question: A conveyor test launches a carton of 16000 grams along the rollers. The carton's launch speed in metres per second is found by taking 5 times the sum of 5 and 3 and then subtracting a slip loss of 25 from the result. The bench records the energy the carton carries because of its motion and multiplies it by 6, because 6 cartons go out in a batch. A fixed instrument offset of 6 J is added to the batch total. What number, in joules, does the bench report?

A launcher brings a sled of 42 kg up to speed along a level track. A base value in metres per second is what the rate curve 3t^2 + 1t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 3 seconds starting from zero, with t the time in seconds, and adding a drive contribution of 30 to that base gives the sled's speed. The logger records the energy the sled carries because of its motion, subtracts a friction allowance of 18 J, and expresses the remainder in kilojoules. The track is 100 m long, a length the logger never uses. What value, in kilojoules, does the logger report?

A test rig launches a carrier of 49000 grams along its rail. The carrier's position in metres is modelled by the fitted curve 1x^3 + 6x^2, with x the time in seconds, and the rate at which that fitted curve is changing at the instant x = 1 second gives a base value. Adding a drive contribution of 22 to that base, and then a further booster contribution of 18, gives the launch speed in metres per second. The rig records the energy the carrier holds because of its motion and multiplies it by 9 for the 9 launches in a run, and by 6 for the 6 runs in the programme. What total, in joules, does the rig report?

A crash-test facility launches a trolley of 47000 grams, and its launch speed in metres per second is 2 times the sum of 7 and 13. The logger records the energy the trolley carries because of its motion and multiplies it by 9, because 9 trolleys go out in a run. The run total is expressed in kilojoules, a standing instrument allowance of 26 kJ is added, and the result is multiplied by 10 for the 10 runs in the programme. The track is 75 m long, a length the logger never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the logger report?

A conveyor test launches a carton of 15000 grams along the rollers, and the carton's launch speed in metres per second is 2 times the sum of 4 and 3. The bench records the energy the carton carries because of its motion, subtracts a friction allowance of 28 J, and then adds a calibration offset of 12 J. The result is multiplied by 10, because 10 cartons go out in a batch, and a standing allowance of 13 J is added to the batch total. The roller bed is 8 m long, a dimension the bench never uses. What number, in joules, does the bench report?

A teaching bench releases a trolley of 56 kg along a level rail. The trolley's release speed in metres per second is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 18 = 0. The bench records the energy the trolley carries because of its motion and expresses that record in kilojoules. The converted figure is multiplied by 7 for the 7 releases in a demonstration, a standing allowance of 12 kJ is added, and a contractual credit of 17 kJ is then subtracted. The rail stands 1 m above the floor, a height the bench never uses. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A press slide carries a tool of 30000 grams, and the tool's position in metres is modelled by the fitted curve 1x^3 + 1x^2, with x the time in seconds. The rate at which that fitted position curve is changing at the instant x = 1 second gives a base value, and multiplying it by 11 for the eleven-stage linkage gives the acceleration in metres per second squared. The controller works out the force needed for that acceleration, adds a die preload of 15 N, and expresses the result in kilonewtons. A contractual credit of 5 kN is then subtracted. The slide is 2 m long, a dimension the controller never uses. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?

A workshop counts 256 rivets in one bin and 181 in another, and the technician works out the largest whole number that divides both counts exactly with nothing left over. He multiplies that number by 8 for the eight channels of his rig, then by 5 for the five-stage booster, and the result is the launch speed in metres per second of a slug of 10000 grams. The bench records the energy the slug holds because of its motion and adds a fixed instrument offset of 19 J. The total is then expressed in kilojoules. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A plant figure is 3 times an adjusted reading, because 3 lines run together. The adjusted reading is a converted force with a contractual credit of 4 kN subtracted from it. That converted force is the kilonewton form of the force needed to drive a slide of 19 kg, with a bearing preload of 9 N added before the conversion. The slide's acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 4t^2 + 1t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds, starting from zero, with t the time in seconds. What is the plant figure, in kilonewtons?

A workshop ledger closes with a number in kilonewtons, converted from a bench figure. That bench figure is what remains after a mounting tare of 12 N and then a frame tare of 11 N are taken from a reading, and that reading was a bearing preload of 24 N added to the force needed to accelerate a carrier of 72 kg. The carrier's acceleration in metres per second squared is the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 9x + 8 = 0. The bench is 1.7 m wide, a dimension the ledger never uses. What number, in kilonewtons, closes the ledger?

A press-shop total is 2 times a hall figure, because two halls report together, and each hall figure is 11 times a line value. Each line value is itself 2 times a converted single-press reading, since two presses share a line. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to drive a ram of 134000 grams, and the ram's acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 1t^2 + 7t accumulates between t = 3 seconds and t = 4 seconds, starting from zero at t = 3 seconds, with t the time in seconds. What is the press-shop total, in kilonewtons?

A press line drives a tool of 14000 grams, and the tool's acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 3t^2 + 2t accumulates between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds, starting from zero at t = 1 second, with t the time in seconds. The controller works out the force needed to drive the tool and multiplies it by 4 for the 4 tools on a press, by 9 for the 9 presses on the line, and by 12 for the 12 lines in the plant. What figure, in newtons, does the controller report?

A rolling mill drives a carrier of 56000 grams along its bed. The rate at which the carrier's acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 2t^2 + 6t, and between t = 2 seconds and t = 4 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero at the start of that interval, giving the acceleration the mill uses. From the force needed to drive the carrier the controller subtracts a bearing tare of 22 N, then adds a mounting allowance of 15 N, and finally adds a further rigging allowance of 5 N. What figure, in newtons, does the controller report?

A conveyor drive accelerates a crate of 127000 grams along the rollers, and the acceleration in metres per second squared is the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 11. The controller works out the force needed for one push and multiplies it by 6, because 6 pushers act together. The total is expressed in kilonewtons, and a fixed frame allowance of 12 kN is added. The roller bed is 10 m long, a dimension the controller never uses. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report?

A shunting yard accelerates a wagon of 140000 grams, and the rate at which its acceleration builds, in metres per second cubed, follows 1t^2 + 8t. Between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds the acceleration accumulates from zero, and the value reached at t = 2 seconds is the one used. The controller works out the force needed to accelerate the wagon and expresses it in kilonewtons. It multiplies that converted figure by 4 for the 4 wagons in a rake, by 8 for the 8 rakes in a shift, and by 12 for the 12 shifts in the cycle. What figure, in kilonewtons, does the controller report for the cycle?

A launch bench brings a carriage of 55000 grams up to speed along a level rail, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 5t^2 + 5t between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds, starting from rest, with t the time in seconds. The bench records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion at the end of that interval and expresses it in kilojoules. The converted figure is multiplied by 7 for the 7 launches in a programme, a standing instrument allowance of 16 kJ is added, and a further ground-station allowance of 14 kJ is added after that. What figure, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A shaker bench fits the curve 5x^3 - 4x^2 to a recorded trace, with x the time in seconds. At the instant x = 2 seconds the rate at which the slope of that fitted curve is itself changing gives, in metres per second, the speed of a test mass of 31000 grams on the head. The bench records the energy the mass carries because of its motion and expresses that record in kilojoules. The converted figure is multiplied by 12, because 12 benches report together, and a fixed calibration offset of 23 kJ is added at the end. What value, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A linear test rig in a materials lab drives a small trolley along a rail, and the trolley's speed is given, in metres per second, by 5*t^3 + 3*t^2 with t in seconds. The trolley assembly has a mass of 2000 g. The engineers are interested in the instant t = 1 s, when the drive must supply exactly the force needed to produce the trolley's rate of change of speed. A calibration spring in the coupling adds a constant 26 N on top of that force. The control panel reports the resulting coupling load in kilonewtons. A full production line contains 12 identical rigs pulling together on a shared support frame, and that frame is itself pre-tensioned to 3 kN. What total load, in kN, does the support frame carry?

On a packaging line a shuttle is driven along its rail by 3 identical magnetic stages. Each stage raises the shuttle's speed by 9 m/s while it charges and by a further 7 m/s while it discharges. Once the shuttle leaves the last stage a spring kicker adds another 4 m/s, and the shuttle then travels at that speed. The loaded shuttle has a mass of 59000 g. A latch at the end of the rail holds a further 12 J, which is added to the shuttle's energy of motion to give the figure logged for one shuttle. Each line runs 11 shuttles at once, and the plant operates 9 identical lines. What total energy, in J, does the plant have in play at that moment?

A crane maker needs the total pull, in kilonewtons, carried by one bank of gantry hoists. Each hoist drives a carriage whose speed along its beam is, in metres per second, 3*t^3 + 0*t^2 with t in seconds. The carriage assembly has a mass of 168000 g. At the instant t = 1 s the drive supplies exactly the force needed to produce the carriage's rate of change of speed, and a counterweight relieves 10 N of that force. The relieved figure is what the maker records for one hoist, expressed in kilonewtons. A bank contains 8 identical hoists working together. What total pull, in kN, does the bank carry?

A conveyor's high-speed drive is being commissioned. The carriage's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, satisfies a^2 - 12a + 32 = 0, and the high-speed setting corresponds to the larger of the two values that fit. The moving carriage has a mass of 138 kg, and the control cabinet beside it is held at 21 degrees C. The drive must supply exactly the force needed to give the carriage that rate of change of speed, and the commissioning sheet records that force in kilonewtons. One bank contains 8 such carriages pulling together, and a counter-tension of 26 kN acts against the bank in the opposite direction. The plant has 3 identical banks. What is the plant's net figure, in kN?

An automation supplier is quoting the total thrust, in newtons, that one of its transfer lines can deliver. Each pusher on the line has a ramp rate r, in m/s^2 per notch, given by the smaller value that satisfies r^2 - 9r + 8 = 0. The controller always runs a pusher at 6 notches, so the moving assembly's actual rate of change of speed is 6 times that ramp rate. The moving assembly of a single pusher has a mass of 173000 g, and each pusher supplies exactly the force that produces this motion. One frame carries 5 pushers, and the line is built from 5 identical frames. What total thrust, in N, does the line deliver?

In a lift-testing tower the cage's rate of change of speed a, in m/s^2, is the smaller value satisfying a^2 - 9a + 18 = 0. The cage and its frame together have a mass of 159000 g, and the hoist supplies exactly the force needed to produce that motion. The load cell in the rope is offset, so 14 N must be taken off the hoist's force to obtain the reading. A guide brush then drags off a further 6 N from that reading. Each shaft is fitted with 3 identical cages, and the tower has 9 shafts. What total reading, in N, does the tower log across every cage?

A logistics depot runs powered carts on a short straight test loop. On the loop a cart's speed v, in m/s, is the smaller value that satisfies v^2 - 12v + 32 = 0. A loaded cart has a mass of 41 kg, and the loop is kept at 18 degrees C for the trial. The cart's energy of motion is measured, and 23 J is deducted from it for the wheel losses. The depot records the deducted figure in kilojoules and multiplies it by the 3 carts it runs together. A charged buffer battery contributes a further 3 kJ to the depot's stored total. What is the depot's stored total, in kJ?

A gear shop is cutting a matched pair of timing belts. One belt has 151 teeth and the other has 33 teeth, and the setter needs the largest whole number of teeth that divides both counts exactly, since that fixes the repeat length of the marking pattern. The test carriage is then run at a speed, in metres per second, numerically equal to that number. The carriage has a mass of 40000 g. Its energy of motion is measured, 4 J is subtracted for the bearing loss, and the corrected figure is multiplied by the 7 identical carriages on the rig. A pre-charged latch then contributes a further 15 J to the rig's total. What is the rig's total figure, in kJ?
